title: Insights into longevity and virus-driven adaptation from Myotis bat genomes.

verified.what_i_actually_checked: Dryad API metadata for doi:10.5061/dryad.02v6wwqfh (version 5, CC0 licence, 3.31 GB total): 16 files, including a 1.82 GB tarball of codon alignments for 536 mammals, a 13 MB aBSREL (a branch-site test for positive selection) omega table, an 89.7 MB bats-only aBSREL table, six VIP (virus-interacting protein) alignment tarballs (52–452 MB each), four ~0.6 MB gene-to-human-homologue text files, and a README. Every file download failed: the Dryad API returned 401 Unauthorized and the web file stream returned 403 Forbidden, so no file contents were opened. The GitHub annotation repo (docmanny/myotis-gene-annotations) exists and holds GFF3 (gene annotation) files.
verified.what_came_from_paper_text_only: aBSREL run on 15,734 gene alignments across 536 mammals; a VIP list of 5,527 genes, extended from a previously published set of 5,291; on average 20,869 protein-coding genes per genome; the DNA-damage (neocarzinostatin) dose-response experiment used primary fibroblasts from 5 bat species; Supplementary Tables 1–9 contents. The Europe PMC supplementary-files request timed out, so the supplement was not retrievable.

a1_downloadable.note: I saw the file listing (public, CC0 licence), but downloading the files without a browser failed (401/403), so I never opened them. Download status is unverified, not confirmed broken.

a2_label_is_a_column.note: The paper has no measured per-item label at scale. The candidate per-gene labels are either selection-test outputs (aBSREL/BUSTED-MH, which test for positive selection) or VIP (virus-interacting protein) membership. The VIP list is assembled from earlier literature and would have to be joined to the genes; it is not among the listed Dryad files (paper text only).

a3_inputs_present.note: The codon alignments themselves are deposited (1.82 GB tarball, from the listing), so the inputs are present rather than referenced.

a4_units_stated.note: Not checked, because the files were never opened. Omega (the dN/dS ratio of protein-changing to silent mutations) and p-values have no units.

a5_enough_rows.note: About 15,734 genes per the paper, which would be enough if a real label existed. The only directly measured phenotypes (DNA-damage tolerance, RNA-seq) cover 5 bat cell lines, far too few.

a6_fits_laptop.working_set: ~0.1 GB of selection tables; 1.8 GB if the alignments are used
a6_fits_laptop.note: Sizes come from the Dryad listing.

a7_counts_match_paper.note: Could not compare, since the files were not opened.

a8_label_provenance.note: Positive-selection calls and omega values are computed by aBSREL from the deposited alignments. Predicting them from sequence or alignment features would just re-learn a statistical test, which is circular. The VIP label is a measurement from earlier literature (physical virus–host interaction), not something this paper produced.

existing_models.name: DeepViral (Bioinformatics 2021): predicts human–virus protein interactions from sequence plus infection phenotypes
STEP (Patterns 2022): a Siamese network on ProtBERT protein-language-model embeddings for virus–host protein interactions
DeepGNHV (Briefings in Bioinformatics 2025): a graph neural network combining a protein language model with AlphaFold2 structures for human–virus protein interactions

backbone.name: ESM-2, a protein language model (only relevant for the rejected VIP-classification idea)

integration.partner_dataset: Zoonomia / TOGA ortholog sets; published VIP list (Enard and Petrov)
integration.join_key: human gene symbol via the *_genes_human-homolog.txt files
integration.bigger_question_one_sentence: Do bat-specific selection signatures plus protein embeddings predict which human proteins interact with viruses better than embeddings alone?

honest_claim_h3: A model could, at best, reproduce aBSREL's selection calls or a literature-curated VIP list, not a physical measurement made in this paper.

plain_idea.one_liner: Use how fast each bat gene evolved, plus its protein sequence, to predict whether the protein physically interacts with viruses.
plain_idea.train_on: One row per gene: evolutionary-rate and selection statistics across 536 mammals, plus a protein-sequence embedding. About 15,734 genes per the paper; not verified, because the files were not opened.
plain_idea.predict: Whether the gene's protein is a known virus-interacting protein. The answer comes from an earlier literature-curated list of 5,527 genes, not from a measurement in this paper.
plain_idea.why_worthwhile: Evolutionary biologists studying virus-host arms races could prioritise genes for testing. But the label is borrowed, and the selection features are computed outputs, so the project's value is limited.

ml_idea: Rejected. The only per-gene targets are selection-test outputs, which are computed from the deposited alignments (circular), or VIP membership from an earlier curated list that is not in the deposit. The measured phenotypes cover 5 cell lines.

effort.compute_note: Not estimated because the project was rejected at Part A; sizes come from the Dryad listing only.
effort.cheapest_killing_check: Open the Dryad README and check whether a per-gene VIP label column is deposited at all.

verdict_reason: Fails A2 and A8. This is a comparative-genomics paper whose per-gene results (aBSREL positive-selection calls, omega values) are statistics computed from the deposited alignments, so predicting them is circular. The virus-interacting-protein label is a borrowed literature list that is not among the deposited files, and the real measurements cover only 5 cell lines. The Dryad files also refused non-browser download (401/403), so I never opened them.
